items.text: Saudi civil defence says a [[p:Houthis|Houthi]] drone hit a tower in Riyadh's financial district on 24 Nov, injuring at least 11; witnesses told AFP it was the [[p:Public Investment Fund]] skyscraper. The Saudi-led coalition then struck Hodeidah port and targets in Saada and Amran, and says it downed seven more drones over Ras Tanura and the Eastern Province on 25 Nov. Houthi spokesman [[p:Yahya Saree]] told workers and shipping to leave all Saudi Red Sea ports, including Jeddah. Mediators Qatar and Pakistan condemned the Riyadh strike.
items.notes: Bloomberg link paywalled. Injury figure from Saudi civil defence via Al Jazeera/AFP/Reuters.

items.text: [[p:Donald Trump]] told the New York Post the Iran campaign is funded to the end of January and his options may narrow once Democrats control Congress; he called Israel's goal of regime change 'probably doable' but not his own aim. Early on 25 Nov the [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|IRGC]] Navy claimed two tankers on an 'unauthorised route' hit mines and caught fire; no ships were named and UKMTO has not confirmed it. Qatar's prime minister left Washington without a breakthrough.
items.notes: Trump remarks Reported; tanker mine strikes Claimed by the IRGC only. Iran October inflation 88.7% (The National).

items.text: The [[p:Office of the United States Trade Representative|USTR]] is about to announce higher tariffs on 16 economies, including China, the EU and Japan, over subsidised industrial overcapacity, AP and Bloomberg report from unnamed sources. The duties would come from a [[e:Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974|Section 301]] probe and partly replace tariffs the Supreme Court struck down in February. Bloomberg says they will be targeted and stay within existing deal levels. Rates and timing are undisclosed; USTR did not comment.
items.notes: Anonymous sources; no formal USTR announcement as of 25 Nov. Second link is AP (Rugaber, Madhani, Boak).

items.text: Xinhua says the [[p:Central Commission for Discipline Inspection]] is investigating Shanghai party secretary and Politburo member [[p:Chen Jining]] {{note: Environmental engineer and former Tsinghua University president who was Beijing mayor from 2017 before taking over Shanghai in 2022.}} for 'serious violations of discipline and law'. AP, citing Eurasia Group, counts him as the fourth Politburo member to fall this term, after [[p:Zhang Youxia]], He Weidong and [[p:Ma Xingrui]]. Taiwanese analysts quoted by CNA say it upends line-up planning for the 2027 Party Congress.
items.notes: CNA analysis (Mandarin, Lu Chia-jung): https://www.cna.com.tw/news/acn/202611240307.aspx. SCMP also (paywalled).

items.text: China's commerce ministry extended to 27 Jan 2027 its suspension of the ban on exporting gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard-material dual-use items to the US, which was due to lapse on 27 Nov. This is a separate track from the suspension of rare-earth curbs and the 24% tariff, which still run to 10 Jan.
items.notes: Official MOFCOM announcement reported by state media.

items.text: Taiwan's TAIEX fell 4.8% to 38,195 on 25 Nov, which local media tied to reports of new US Section 301 tariffs and doubts about AI returns. Executive Yuan spokesperson Lee Hui-chih said Taipei expects its 15% non-stacking rate under its US trade agreement to hold (CNA, translated).
items.notes: Index figure from ETtoday (Chen Ying-hsin).

items.text: Prosecutors indicted [[p:Taiwan People's Party]] Taoyuan council candidate Zhou Xiaoyun under the Anti-Infiltration Act, alleging she took Chinese Communist Party-linked money and collected personal data and face photos for a troll network. The [[p:Mainland Affairs Council]] called Beijing's election interference a serious national security issue; [[p:Ko Wen-je]] called the case judicial double standards.
items.notes: Translated from Chinese. Allegations are the prosecution case; trial pending.

items.text: In the final week before the 28 Nov [[e:2026 Taiwanese local elections]], 19.58 million voters choose 11,051 posts, and a referendum asks whether to drop the 'nuclear-free homeland' policy. [[p:Lai Ching-te]] urged turnout on 25 Nov; in Taipei, Mayor [[p:Chiang Wan-an]] and the DPP's [[p:Puma Shen]] clashed over child and food safety. A poll blackout applies in the last 10 days.
items.notes: Lai remarks: https://www.cna.com.tw/news/aipl/202611250188.aspx

items.text: Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi said the timing of a $14bn US arms package, including Patriot missiles and a 360-degree radar, is 'very much up to' Trump, who froze it in May as trade leverage. No approval was reported after the Shenzhen summit.

Coverage of [[e:APEC China 2026]] shows [[p:Sanae Takaichi]], the first Japanese leader in China since 2019, got only a greeting-line handshake from Xi, who did not reply. She declined to say how Japan would respond to a Taiwan contingency. China's seafood ban, travel warnings and dual-use export curbs on Japan stay in place.
items.notes: Taiwan contingency remark: https://focustaiwan.tw/politics/202611190020

items.text: Ahead of the 26 Nov anniversary of the [[e:Wang Fuk Court fire]], which killed 168, the government said it will hold no official memorial, will allow 'lawful' events and will act against 'destructive acts'. It announced HK$630m in new grants for victims. A commentary from Beijing's Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office warned against exploiting the disaster to destabilise the city.
items.notes: Police also arrested 97 in a HK$130m building-maintenance bid-rigging case (headline only).

items.text: Macau's legislature unanimously passed the outline of the 2027 budget, with a 715m pataca surplus and stamp duty restored on large-event tickets.

The [[p:State Great Khural]] voted 96 of 104 to accept President [[p:Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh]]'s resignation with immediate effect, the first by a sitting Mongolian president, Euronews reports. He denies taking about $25m over a 2019 railway contract. Speaker Byambatsogt is acting president, and an election must be held within four months.
items.notes: Second link is AP via Beta/N1 (Serbian). Khürelsükh also called for a constitutional referendum alongside the election.

items.text: PM N. Uchral said the presidential election date will be set before 20 Dec and that the [[p:Mongolian People's Party]] nominee must have no criminal record (ikon.mn, translated).

Ruling for the first time on the question, the full bench of the [[p:Supreme Court of Korea]] held that the [[e:2024 South Korean martial law]] was an insurrection. But it found ex-PM [[p:Han Duck-soo]]'s push for a pre-declaration cabinet meeting did not prove intent and sent that part back to the Seoul High Court, upholding other convictions. Three justices dissented. Han stays in detention.
items.notes: Bears on Yoon Suk Yeol appeal verdict due 26 Jan 2027 (W-261111-05).

items.text: The Supreme Court made final the four-year sentence of former first lady [[p:Kim Keon Hee]] for stock manipulation and taking luxury gifts from a former Unification Church official. A separate bribery case is still pending.

[[p:Lee Jae Myung]] nominated Lim Woong-soon as foreign minister, [[p:Hong Ihk-pyo]] as unification minister and ex-justice minister [[p:Kang Kum-sil]] to head the [[p:National Intelligence Service (South Korea)|NIS]]. NK News and Bloomberg link the shake-up to the North Korea deadlock and strained US ties; Segye reads Lim's pick as putting the US alliance first.
items.notes: Bloomberg also (paywalled). Korean press reports a row over Lim's military service; the foreign ministry says he served properly.

items.text: [[p:Kim Jong Un]] personally received credentials from ten new ambassadors, including Russia's, India's and Indonesia's, for the first time, NK News reports. KCNA quotes him saying the North seeks security, not supremacy. It follows his silence on Trump's offers to meet.
items.notes: Content is KCNA's account.

items.text: [[p:Rafael Grossi]] told the IAEA board that an extension of the enrichment plant at the [[p:Yongbyon Nuclear Scientific Research Center|Yongbyon]] complex, begun in mid-September and finished by late October, is 'extremely worrying'. The agency tracks the site by satellite.
Kim called a powerful navy 'the foremost strategic task' at a naval college in Hamhung and toured factories and farms; analysts quoted by SBS read the tours as a signal he is ignoring Trump.
items.notes: KCNA account.

items.text: Six upper-house opposition parties, including the [[p:Constitutional Democratic Party of Japan|CDP]] and [[p:Komeito]], agreed to file a censure motion against Education Minister Seki Yoshihiro over undisclosed 2024 fundraising parties and to stall bills, including the food consumption-tax cut, until he goes. [[p:Sanae Takaichi]] says she will not dismiss him (Kyodo/Nippon.com, translated).
items.notes: The 24 Nov censure agreement comes from an English Kyodo rewrite on a minor site; original Kyodo text not found.

items.text: Police named ex-national police chief [[p:Listyo Sigit Prabowo]] and five officers as treason suspects in the case of wiretapping [[p:Prabowo Subianto]], after raids at 14 sites. Police allege a plot from Oct 2024 that moved to surveillance, 'cyber troop' campaigns and protest mobilisation; the charge carries up to death. The Jakarta Post calls Listyo a [[p:Joko Widodo]] loyalist.
items.notes: Translated from Indonesian. Allegations are the police case.

items.text: Prabowo nominated Coordinating Minister Sugiono and Agriculture Minister [[p:Andi Amran Sulaiman]] to the [[p:People's Consultative Assembly]] to replace [[p:Gibran Rakabuming Raka]] as vice president. The MPR vote has moved twice and is now set for 11 Dec; the Supreme Court cleared both candidates' records.
items.notes: Translated from Indonesian.

items.text: [[p:Bank Indonesia]] raised its policy rate 25 basis points to 6.00%, its first hike since June, to defend a rupiah down about 8% this year.

The [[p:International Court of Justice]] found Myanmar responsible for the [[e:Rohingya genocide]] and for failing to prevent and punish it, in the case brought by The Gambia; it is the first such finding against a state. It ordered prosecutions, guarantees of non-repetition and safe return, with compensation to be set later.
items.notes: Reports that China rejected the ruling and the UK expelled a junta attaché come from a digest and are unverified.

items.text: President [[p:Min Aung Hlaing]] told parliament Myanmar is reconsidering its ties with [[p:ASEAN]], which he said pressures only his country, after its exclusion from the Manila summit. He announced a peace conference for February.
items.notes: Bloomberg paywalled.

items.text: [[p:Anwar Ibrahim]] said he has not accepted [[p:Anthony Loke]]'s resignation, that Loke is on leave, and that the government has more than a year left, an implicit rebuff to Deputy PM [[p:Ahmad Zahid Hamidi]]'s call for early polls. Loke still says he is resigning.

The [[p:International Criminal Court]] says the prosecution will call about 100 witnesses in [[p:Rodrigo Duterte]]'s crimes-against-humanity trial, which opens on 30 Nov; more than 500 victims may take part.

Vice President [[p:Sara Duterte]]'s Senate impeachment trial paused until 1 Dec; Presiding Officer [[p:Francis Escudero]] set hearings through 17 Dec, and the Manila Times reports a verdict could come 16–18 Dec.

The Philippine armed forces counted 48 Chinese vessels in the West Philippine Sea on 17–23 Nov, up from 19 during the ASEAN summit week, and a PLA [[p:Xian H-6|H-6]] bomber flew between [[p:Scarborough Shoal]] and Luzon on 21 Nov. Spokesperson Roy Vincent Trinidad called it a show of force.
items.notes: AFP (Armed Forces of the Philippines) figures.

items.text: An appeals court upheld the lèse-majesté conviction of opposition MP [[p:Rukchanok Srinork]], halving her sentence to three years; she loses her seat if bail is denied.
items.notes: Unbylined, labelled AI-assisted. Censure debate against 18 ministers set provisionally for 7–10 Dec (Nation).

items.text: [[p:Hun Sen]] said Cambodia will take the border dispute to international forums, citing no joint surveys for 11 months; Thailand demanded full implementation of the Dec 2025 joint statement. No clashes were reported.

The National Assembly closed its session after passing 38 laws, the 2027 budget and a growth target of at least 10%; [[p:Tô Lâm]] signed retirement decisions for former Politburo members including [[p:Phạm Minh Chính]].
items.notes: State media.
